terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A one-piece moulding: nothing opens, turns or swings, nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets. A hundred of these round a beer garden is the design case, so the single draw call is the design constraint. Cream-white polypropylene scuffed grey, a rust-yellow stain at the top of the back, black foot caps; stacked in towers when not in use.

reasoning: ONE component on ONE material -- ONE draw call of two: the seat pan (a flattened 20-segment cylinder), the apron and four legs (tapered sweeps), the lower back band and five fan slats, two arms with their front panels and rear uprights, the stain, 36 perforation marks and eight dots, four foot caps, all merged.
One material: cream polypropylene at 0.50 as a vertex colour on a WHITE material, the apron a shade lower, perforations mid-grey, foot caps dark, and a 256 px grime canvas after construction.
No repetition system at one draw call: five slats and 36 perforation marks are boxes inside the single merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the fan of five slats leaning back over a solid lower band, arms that run straight down into the front legs, a dished seat with the radial perforation pattern, and fin legs tapering to dark caps. A slatted seat or straight vertical back would be a different chair; the perforation pattern is what says monobloc rather than garden bench.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The perforations are recessed marks, not holes: 36 thin mid-grey boxes 0.5 mm proud of the seat. Real slots would cost triangles and the hole gate, and at prop distance a dark recess and a hole read alike; declared as a substitution.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.59 x 0.80 x 0.57 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

silhouette.description: A 0.59 m wide moulding: seat pan topping at 0.45 inside a 0.47 x 0.41 apron from 0.36; a lower back band from 0.44 to 0.60 leaning 24 degrees with five fan slats above it to 0.80, feet 85 mm apart and spreading 7 degrees each; arms 0.085 wide at 0.60-0.63 running from the band to z +0.27 and dropping as 0.12-deep panels into the front legs; four fin legs 0.040 x 0.060 at the foot widening to 0.079 x 0.120 (front) and 0.056 x 0.120 (rear) under the seat.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-0.295 at the arms, y 0 to 0.812 at the outer slat tops, z -0.311 at the top of the back to +0.285 at the arm fronts. Declared 0.55 x 0.80 x 0.55 (w/h = d/h 0.6875). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.404 x 1.899 x 1.351, w/h 0.739 and d/h 0.712 -- inside tolerance but 7% wider -- so with height as the trustworthy axis (a monobloc armchair is 0.78-0.82 m) the plan is 0.80 x 0.739 = 0.59 by 0.80 x 0.712 = 0.57, and the declaration was corrected to match. Stations off the proxy (occupancy, 50 rows of H, 80 columns of W): back slats rows 0.82-0.98 across 0.71 W with gaps at columns 34 and 45, their z range from 0.18 H at 0.82 to 0.04 H at 0.98 (a ~29-degree lean, built at 24 so the top stays inside D); arms rows 0.72-0.80 the full width, 0.40 m long, 0.09 wide each; seat rows 0.48-0.56 (top 0.45 m) over 0.84 W by z 0.17-0.69 H; an apron rows 0.40-0.46; a solid lower back rows 0.58-0.70; front legs at x +-0.44 W and z 0.60 H, rear legs at z 0.10 H, both as fins whose webs (columns 8-20) taper from row 0.46 to 0.00.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.404 x 1.899 x 1.351, w/h 0.739 and d/h 0.712, which widened the declared plan 7%. Every station above is the proxy band table in fractions of H; the plate settled the slat count (five), the perforation pattern and the arm section, which the 20 mm voxel fuses.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED. The back of the slats and the rear legs are hidden; built as the mirror of the front with the rear fins narrower, confidence 0.8.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Seat pan r 0.228 x 0.86 in z, 0.020 thick topping at 0.45; apron 0.42 x 0.36 -> 0.47 x 0.41 from 0.36 to 0.445; back band 0.50 wide from 0.44 to 0.60 leaning 24 degrees; five slats 0.078-0.090 wide, 0.022 thick, from 0.58 to 0.80 along the lean, spreading 7 degrees each; arms 0.085 x 0.030 at 0.60 with 0.12-deep front panels down to the apron; front legs 0.040 x 0.060 -> 0.079 x 0.120 and rear legs -> 0.056 x 0.120, 0.368 tall; caps 0.042 x 0.014 x 0.062.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The seat pan sits inside the apron's rim as interpenetrating solids; the leg tops run 20 mm up into the apron; the arm panels meet the legs as opposed faces; slats stand 2 mm proud of the band's top edge; perforations, stain and caps are proud by their own thickness. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.45 m.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the chair envelope. The shipped compound is DERIVED from the geometry by scripts/derive-colliders.mjs.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/back.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: the arms, the seat and the top of the back
localOverrides.evidence: crops/arm.png -- grey scuff marks along the arm; crops/back.png -- a rust-yellow stain at the top of the left slat. Carried as the grime canvas and a proud stain box.

evidence: Measured on the plate: lit plastic #f3f2ef / #fafaf9 (242-250), back slats #d8d5bf (211), legs in shade #d0c5a7 (197), arm shade #ece0bf (224); analyze_texture meanLum 199 sat 0.16 on the back and 180 with specularFraction 0.45 on the arm; extract_pbr_evidence palette #DAD3B1 #454034 #EDE4C2 #CEC295 #AAA483 at confidence 0.86 on both crops.

Textureless as DECLARED: cream 0xefeadc as a vertex colour, apron 0xd9d3c2, perforations 0x8f8474 (luma 132 at saturation 0.19 -- clear of the gate's backdrop band), foot caps 0x6a5a4a (black in the plate, lifted on chroma), the stain 0xd9c9a2, and a 256 px grime canvas after construction.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: plastic only: 1 of 2; every tone is a vertex colour on it.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 872 of 2000: a 20-segment flattened cylinder, five tapered sweeps, forty-five boxes and eight 6-segment discs.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A flattened cylinder for the seat pan; tapered sweeps (frusta) for the apron and legs; rotated boxes for the band, slats, arms, perforations, stain and caps; small discs for the dot perforations.
No InstancedMesh at one draw call. In a scene the HOST instances the chair -- by the hundred.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 256 px grime canvas after construction, 0.25 MB; the factory built in under 50 ms.

risks.description: The seat pattern is recessed marks, not openings.
risks.mitigation: Declared as a substitution; 36 proud mid-grey boxes and discs read as slots at prop distance.

risks.description: The four gaps between the fan slats and the openings under the arms enclose backdrop at every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: Real openings: --allow-holes on the holeviz and _holecc measurements.

risks.description: A monobloc's arm is one curved flow into the leg; boxes and sweeps can read as a wooden chair.
risks.mitigation: The first build did; the arm front panel now shares the leg's x and z and its section, and the leg's top section matches the panel, so they read as one moulding.
